user.title: Where will your photos be stored?
user.description:
freedomCam saves camera snapshots in **your own** S3-compatible bucket. Nobody else sees them.

If you have no storage yet, Cloudflare R2 is a good start: 10 GB free and no charge for downloading photos to your phone. Backblaze B2 does not ask for a card to start.

cloudflare_r2.title: Cloudflare R2
cloudflare_r2.description:
1. In the Cloudflare dashboard open **R2** (it asks for a card even on the free plan) and create a bucket, e.g. `freedomcam`.
2. Copy your **Account ID** (R2 overview, right column).
3. **Manage API tokens → Create API token** with permission **Object Read & Write** for that bucket. Copy the *Access Key ID* and *Secret Access Key* (shown only once).

Tip: a token with **Admin Read & Write** also lets freedomCam set the retention for you.

[Cloudflare guide]({help_url})

data_description.jurisdiction: Only change it if you created the bucket in the EU or FedRAMP jurisdiction.

aws_s3.title: Amazon S3
aws_s3.description:
1. Create a bucket in the region you prefer.
2. In IAM create a user with a policy that allows `s3:PutObject`, `s3:GetObject`, `s3:DeleteObject` and `s3:ListBucket` on that bucket (and `s3:PutLifecycleConfiguration` if you want freedomCam to set the retention).
3. Create an **access key** for that user.

[AWS guide]({help_url})

backblaze_b2.title: Backblaze B2
backblaze_b2.description:
1. Create a **private** bucket.
2. Its details show the **S3 endpoint**, e.g. `s3.eu-central-003.backblazeb2.com`: the region is the middle part (`eu-central-003`).
3. **Application Keys → Add a New Application Key**, restricted to that bucket with *Read and Write* access. Copy the *keyID* and *applicationKey*.

[Backblaze guide]({help_url})

wasabi.title: Wasabi
wasabi.description:
1. Create a bucket and note its region (e.g. `eu-central-1`).
2. Create a user with access keys and a policy limited to that bucket.

[Wasabi guide]({help_url})

other.title: Other S3-compatible storage
other.description: MinIO, Garage, a NAS with an S3 service, Scaleway, OVH… Enter the endpoint URL of the S3 API (without the bucket).

data.virtual_host: Virtual-hosted addressing (bucket in the host name)

data_description.region: Use `us-east-1` if your service does not use regions.
data_description.virtual_host: Leave it off unless your provider requires `https://bucket.endpoint/` URLs.

retention.title: How long are photos kept?
retention.description: Old photos are deleted by the bucket itself (a lifecycle rule), even if Home Assistant is off.

data.manage_lifecycle: Let freedomCam set the rule in the bucket

data_description.manage_lifecycle: Turn it off if your keys cannot manage the bucket: then set the rule yourself in your provider's console.

reauth_confirm.title: New keys for {bucket}
reauth_confirm.description: The storage rejected the keys. Enter new ones.

error.cannot_connect: Cannot reach the storage. Check the endpoint, region and your connection.
error.invalid_auth: The keys are not valid (check them, and the region).
error.access_denied: The keys work but cannot write to this bucket. Give them read and write permission.
error.bucket_not_found: The bucket does not exist and these keys cannot create it. Create it in your provider's console.
error.cannot_read: The keys can write but cannot read the bucket back. Give them read permission too.
error.lifecycle_denied: These keys cannot manage the bucket rules. Turn off the option and set the retention in your provider's console.
error.lifecycle_failed: This provider did not accept the retention rule. Turn off the option and set it in its console.

data.pause_seconds: Minimum time between photos of a camera
data.max_per_hour: Maximum photos per camera and hour
data.thumbnails: Upload thumbnails (saves mobile data in the app)

data_description.presence_entity: Cameras marked *only when nobody is home* work while this entity is `off`, `not_home` or `0` (e.g. `zone.home`).
data_description.ai_provider: Adds what is in the photo to its name (person, car, dog…). Cloudflare Workers AI has a daily free allowance.
data_description.app_access_key_id: To connect the freedomCam iOS app with a QR code: create **read-only** keys for this bucket and enter them here. The QR code appears as an image entity of the integration.

error.ai_missing: Enter the Account ID and the token to use Cloudflare Workers AI.
error.ai_failed: Cloudflare Workers AI did not answer with these details.
error.app_keys_incomplete: Enter both app keys, or none.
error.app_keys_invalid: The app keys cannot read the bucket.
error.app_keys_can_write: The app keys can WRITE to the bucket. For the phone use read-only keys.

user.title: Add a camera
user.description: **Image** compares each snapshot with the previous ones (any camera). **Motion sensor** takes photos while a binary sensor detects motion (cameras that report motion to Home Assistant).

data_description.camera_id: Lowercase letters, numbers, `-` and `_`. Made from the name if empty. It cannot be changed later.

error.invalid_camera_id: Use lowercase letters, numbers, `-` and `_`, starting with a letter or number.
error.camera_id_taken: Another camera already uses this folder.
